Hi Jane — thanks for the clear list. Drafting the checklist below and attaching a sample invoice + a proposed tranche schedule for your review. See the short answers up front, then a compact checklist at the bottom.

Quick answers:
- Invoice cadence: initial invoice for 40% on signature; then three equal monthly tranches of 20% each (total = 100% prepay). We can convert to quarterly tranches if you prefer longer windows.
- Drawdown evidence: initial invoice = signed MSA; subsequent tranches = invoice referencing PO# + statement of usage (billing ledger snapshot).
- VAT: If you need us to invoice Acme UK Ltd for UK VAT purposes we can do that — we need your VAT registration number and any reverse-charge confirmation from your tax team.
- Wires: Redwoods standard beneficiary details are in the attached schedule (bank-wire-section). Typical settlement: 3 business days after invoice receipt.

Attachments: redwood-prepay-schedule_v2.xlsx (contains wiring, sample invoice, and ledger reference column); sample-invoice-acme.pdf

Checklist (action items for Acme):
1) Confirm billing entity (Acme Corp vs Acme UK Ltd) and provide VAT reg number if UK.
2) Return signed MSA (we'll issue initial invoice at that moment).
3) Provide PO# for invoice reference (we'll include PO on all subsequent invoices).
4) For faster processing, add procureops@acme-corp.com to our invoice approval group (optional).

If this structure works I'll lock the schedule and generate the xls with invoice line items for your controllers. Happy to hop on a 30m call if you want to walk through.

Best,

Hi Jane / Tessa — adding from tax/ops side. A couple operational clarifications from Redwood's finance team that affect invoice form and evidence: 

- VAT: If you request invoicing to Acme UK Ltd, please confirm whether you expect Redwood to charge UK VAT or whether reverse-charge applies. If reverse charge, we'll need a written confirmation from your tax team referencing the specific supply and the VAT reg number.
- Legal entity: invoice must be addressed to the legal name on the PO. If the PO is to Acme Corp (US), we will not add UK VAT.
- Evidence for drawdown: for subsequent tranches we accept either (a) the PO with PO# + an emailed acceptance from the Acme billing contact, or (b) a single consolidated ledger snapshot from your procurement platform showing the reserved balance — whichever is easier for you.
- Banking: for international wires, please add the beneficiary's intermediary bank details to avoid delays. Our bank info in the attached workbook has SWIFT and intermediary fields.

I've attached a short tax-evidence checklist inside the spreadsheet. If Acme's tax team wants to rely on a periodic VAT certificate instead of per-invoice evidence, we can accept that but need it on file before the first tranche.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Finance Ops | Redwood Inference
